Step 1: Understand the dimensions of a Gray Whale. Gray whales are very large marine mammals, typically growing to a length of about 43 to 49 feet (13 to 15 meters) and weighing around 30 to 40 tons.

Step 2: Understand the dimensions of a typical above-ground pool. Standard above-ground pools are usually round or rectangular, with diameters or lengths typically ranging from 12 to 30 feet, and depths of about 4 feet.

Step 3: Compare the sizes. A Gray Whale (43–49 feet long) is significantly longer than the largest standard above-ground pools (around 24–30 feet long). Furthermore, its massive weight and volume would completely overwhelm the structural capacity of a residential above-ground pool.

Step 4: Conclude whether the whale would fit easily. Due to the vast difference in size, a Gray Whale would not fit in an above-ground pool at all, let alone "easily."

Final answer: No
